scenes.say: Ever had your build suddenly fail, just because of one library version? Let's see why dependency management is the heart of Maven and Gradle.

scenes.label: Transitive
scenes.sub: Dependencies pull in their own dependencies—automatically.
scenes.say: Both Maven and Gradle pull in not just your direct dependencies, but also everything those dependencies need. That's called transitive dependencies.
If two libraries need different versions of the same thing, your build only gets one. That can cause bugs or crashes.
To fix this, both tools can use a Bill of Materials, or BOM. It locks dependency versions, making builds predictable and stable.

scenes.question: Can you ignore version conflicts?
scenes.wrong: Sure, the build will pick one.
scenes.right: Ignoring conflicts risks runtime errors or subtle bugs.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: can you just ignore version conflicts? Many do, but that leads to weird runtime errors or subtle bugs.
